01
The story · Cluda · Simpli Automation Ltd, Northern Ireland

Deterministic AI for insurance.

Same documents in, same answer out, every time, with a page reference behind every decision.

Insurance runs on documents: policy wordings, schedules, quotes, renewal terms, commission statements. Every placement, every renewal and every record in a broker's system starts with someone reading them. AI that gives a different answer each time it reads the same document cannot be adopted for regulated work, however good the demo looks.

Cluda is deterministic end to end: the pipeline that reads the documents, the broker workflows it feeds, the extraction that turns documents into structured data, and the policy administration system that holds the record. Policy analysis for employee-benefits brokers is where it starts.

The £2M seed takes Cluda from that first use case to the rest of the broker's work, and to leadership of the category in employee benefits.

02
The problem

Insurance cannot adopt non-deterministic AI.

Liability
A general model asked the same question twice can give two different answers. In insurance a hallucinated clause is an E&O claim: a missed exclusion is an uncovered client and a liable broker, and missed coverage gaps are a leading cause of broker E&O claims.
Accuracy
Before AI can compare, advise or fill in a record, it has to extract the data from policy PDFs: benefits, limits, exclusions and terms spread across tables, footnotes and endorsements. Extraction that is right most of the time is not usable at all, because every figure then has to be checked by hand. It has to be 100% accurate, and general models are not.
Evidence
The FCA's Consumer Duty requires firms to demonstrate, not merely claim, good outcomes, with fair-value analysis done at the time rather than reconstructed later. That needs a page reference behind every decision, and a chat window cannot give one.

So adoption has stalled. Under 5% of brokers use purpose-built AI; the rest paste client data into ChatGPT or Copilot, with zero traceability. The broker's systems (Acturis, SSP, Open GI) store and track policies. They don't read them. Marsh, with the capital and engineers to do it, built its own internal comparison tool. The other 400,000 brokers can't build their own.

03
The problem · Where the time goes

Three jobs take the hours, and all three are reading documents.

Policy analysis
From fact find through quotes and analysis to the market review report, policy analysis is the centre of every placement and renewal. A typical renewal is 6 to 8 hours: getting the quotes, analysing the wordings, building the report.
Data entry
Once the business is placed, what the documents say is keyed again into the policy administration system: the scheme, the benefits, the members, the premiums, the renewal dates, every joiner and leaver. The same data, typed by hand, one more time.
Reconciliation
In the brokerage's finance team, commission statements arrive from each insurer in its own format and are checked against the policies and invoices behind them. Many documents, one answer that has to tie out.

Premiums are down around 20% across most UK commercial lines: brokers must do more with less. Each of these jobs can be handed to AI only if the answer is the same every time and traces to the page it came from.

04
The product · The harness

The harness: how deterministic AI is built.

A model on its own is not something anyone in insurance can trust with the work. Cluda is the harness around the model: four layers, each built on what the one before it produces.

Intelligence layer
Reads and understands the documents. Determinism comes from the ingestion pipeline, not from the model: every document is parsed, structured and checked the same way every time, so the same document always gives the same answer, with the page it came from.
Workflows
The broker's jobs: analysis, placement, renewal. Each is a chain of decisions a broker already makes; Cluda makes each one the same way every time and records why.
Processing layer
Deterministic extraction of structured data from any insurance document (benefits, limits, exclusions, terms, schedules), inside Cluda and, in phase 2, API access for broker PAS and insurer systems.
System of record
The employee-benefits policy administration system, where the record lives and stays consistent with the documents behind it, and where the finance team reconciles commission statements against the policies. Incorporate Benefits is the proof build, switching over in November 2026. Once a broker's records and Consumer Duty evidence run through Cluda, switching is structural, not a matter of convenience.

Determinism has to run through all four for AI to be trusted with the work. A deterministic model feeding an unchecked workflow, or clean extraction landing in a record nobody can trace, breaks the chain. That is why 40% of the raise goes to proprietary model development: the evaluation set and the deterministic pipeline first, then, over time, an insurance-trained model that beats general LLMs on that set at a lower cost per document.

05
The product · The first use case

The first use case: policy analysis.

Policy wordings in, the comparison back in minutes, with a page reference behind every decision. Live for private medical insurance.

1 / 3

The comparison runs on 70,260 product configurations and 8.27 million data points from nine insurer files, each traced to its source page.

Faster
Quote comparison from 30 minutes to 3: around 90% of the analysis time, measured in our broker ROI model. The saving is the by-product; the depth is the point.
Trust channel
AMII chose Cluda for its members. The Association of Medical Insurance Intermediaries is the UK trade body for the brokers who place private medical insurance. Its 106 member firms roll out from November 2026, with the PMI teams at five of the top ten UK brokers in the first wave, several already asking about additional licences. An ex-broker CEO and account manager onboard every firm in person.

The pattern is Harvey's in law, where trust is the product. Harvey won the hardest buyer first: Allen & Overy's 3,500 lawyers asked 40,000 questions before a firm-wide rollout, its first 50 enterprise customers came by referral, and it reached $75M ARR within two years of launch. Insurance has the same shape and nobody has done it. Our trust channel is a trade body, and the hardest firms go first.

06
The product · The ladder

Then the rest of the work, one rung at a time.

£79
Policy analysis. The comparison, six states and a page reference behind every cell. Takes the scan and the Excel sheet off the broker.
£149
Placement and renewal workflow. The analysis inside the whole job, from fact find through quotes to the market review report. Takes the renewal off the broker, not just the comparison.
£249
Policy administration system. The system of record with the comparison built in: data extracted from the documents lands in the record instead of being keyed in, and commission statements are checked against the policies behind them. Takes the data entry off the broker and the reconciliation off the finance team. From May 2027.

Prices are per user per month. The ladder extends across the whole employee-benefits package as each product line comes on in 2027: cash plan, life, dental and wellness alongside private medical insurance, so a broker compares, places and administers the package in one place. A firm starts where its need is and moves up as Cluda takes over more of the work; a firm with no policy administration system starts at the top.

The target: 500 active users at a blended £200 per user per month, £1.2M ARR by the end of 2027.

07
The market

Employee-benefits brokers first. Lead the category, then widen.

Bottom-up. The category is deterministic AI for employee-benefits brokers. The wedge is the UK's specialist employee-benefits and PMI intermediaries, an estimated several hundred firms. AMII's 106 member firms are the reachable core, with five of the top ten UK brokers in the first wave.

AMII is the commercial test case for broker networks. After the UK come the global employee-benefits networks, WBN and Brokerslink among them, then UK broker networks beyond AMII, where early-stage discussions are under way with Bravo Networks (450 broker firms) and Hedron Network for commercial lines. Growth inside each network is product-led: a broker who runs one real placement through Cluda does not go back to the scan. The aim is market leader of the category before widening to other lines.

How the team has changed

The founding team was built to prove the product: a founder from broking, a technical co-founder as CTO, and an early team. It built the prototype, won AMII and Incorporate Benefits, and raised the pre-seed.

2026 needs a different shape: production engineering and security for a rollout to 106 firms, a system of record live at a client, and sales capacity beyond the founder. The team has been rebuilt around that.

  • Engineering leadership. The former CTO left in April 2026. Two founders who have built venture-backed companies through Y Combinator now lead engineering: Ali Shahriyari (Reality Defender, YC W22) on direction and architecture, and Gaurav Thapa (Kodo, YC W21) full-time on delivery, security and platform operations.
  • Operations. Bel Gaia was promoted to COO in August 2026 to run the company day to day, so the CEO's time goes to customers, networks and the round.
  • Sales. Emma O'Murray, a former broker, joins in October 2026 to turn AMII licences into paid seats.
  • Equity follows the work. The former CTO's shares are being transferred to the current leadership and the founder, and the team and advisors hold growth shares. The table as it will stand is in section 08.

Data room · Section 03

What Cluda does, and how it stays deterministic.

The vision, the four layers, the product live today and where it is used.

As at 16 September 2026

Vision

Insurance runs on documents, and AI that gives a different answer each time it reads the same document cannot be used for regulated work. Cluda builds deterministic AI for insurance brokers: the same documents in, the same answer out, a page reference behind every decision. Policy analysis for employee-benefits brokers is the first use case; the plan is to take over the rest of the broker's document work, one rung at a time, and lead the category in employee benefits.

How it works: four layers

A model on its own is not something anyone in insurance can trust with the work. Cluda is the harness around the model, and each layer is built on what the one before it produces.

LayerWhat it doesStatus
IntelligenceReads and understands insurance documents. Determinism comes from the ingestion pipeline: every document parsed, structured and checked the same way every time, with the page each answer came from.Live for private medical insurance
WorkflowsThe broker's jobs (analysis, placement, renewal) as chains of decisions made the same way every time and recorded.Policy analysis live; placement and renewal workflow in 2027

The product today: policy analysis

Policy wordings in, the comparison back in minutes. Live for private medical insurance, built for AMII's member firms. The comparison runs on 70,260 product configurations and 8.27 million data points from nine insurer files, each traced to its source page.

Every cell is one of six coverage states, so a broker sees not just covered or not covered but what applies and where it comes from. The saving is the by-product; the depth is the point.

Where it is used

  • AMII member firms. The UK trade body for health and protection intermediaries. Rollout to all 106 member firms from November 2026, with the PMI teams at five of the top ten UK brokers in the first wave.
  • Incorporate Benefits. An AI-native employee-benefits policy administration system, switching over on 27 November 2026. The proof build for the system-of-record layer.

Security and trust

  • Cyber Essentials held. ISO 27001 certification planned for Q1 2027; SOC 2 where a broker's group procurement requires it.
  • Documents a broker uploads are treated as data, never as instructions: parsing is isolated from any instruction-following step, and anomalies are logged and flagged.
  • Every release is re-run against the same evaluation set. Defects are classified by root cause, fixed once, and locked with a regression test.

What comes next

The whole employee-benefits package comparable in 2027 (cash plan, life, dental and wellness alongside PMI), the placement and renewal workflow, the policy administration system from May 2027, and API access for broker PAS and insurer systems. Milestones and what each needs are in the roadmap (section 04).

Where the time goes: four stages

Every renewal and placement runs through the same four stages. Together they take a broker 6 to 8 hours per case, and every stage is reading documents.

StageWhat the broker does todayWhat Cluda takes off
1. Fact findGathers the client's current scheme, members, benefits and renewal terms from documents and emailsReads the current policy and schedule into structured data. Placement and renewal workflow, 2027
2. QuotesApproaches insurers and collects quotes and wordings, each in the insurer's own formatEach insurer's plans held on their real terms, so options are configured, not re-keyed. Live for private medical insurance
3. Policy analysisScans the wordings and keys covered, not covered and partial into ExcelThe comparison in minutes, a page reference behind every cell. Live for private medical insurance, £79 per user
4. Market review reportBuilds the client report and the Consumer Duty evidence behind the recommendationThe report generated from the comparison, with the audit trail. Placement and renewal workflow, £149 per user, 2027

Cluda takes stage 3 off the broker today and stages 1, 2 and 4 with the placement and renewal workflow in 2027. On stage 3, quote comparison goes from about 30 minutes to about 3 in our broker ROI model: the 90% on the main page. We will publish measured times for each stage from the November rollout.

What we will report

Monthly from the rollout: firms live, active users and paid seats by rung, seats per firm, MRR, time per comparison, and the determinism and accuracy results on the evaluation set. LTV, CAC and retention cohorts follow once there are paying users to measure.

Data room · Section 06

The trade body, the proof build, and the networks next.

What AMII and Incorporate Benefits bought, why they bought it, and the network sequence from here.

As at 16 September 2026

AMII

Who. The Association of Medical Insurance Intermediaries, the UK trade body for health and protection intermediaries: 106 member firms, including five of the top ten UK brokers.

What they bought. A one-year contract, £60,000, signed and paid, within a three-year exclusive partnership in which Cluda is AMII's only AI tool for policy analysis. It covers Cluda's policy analysis across the membership: private medical insurance compared plan by plan on each insurer's real terms, with a page reference behind every line. Each member firm receives one licence in year one; additional seats are £79 per user per month. From year two, member firms buy direct from Cluda.

Why. Members compared insurer wordings by hand on every case. AMII wanted one consistent, auditable comparison for the whole membership, checked against the insurers' own documents, and chose Cluda to provide it.

Where it stands. Rollout to all 106 member firms from November 2026, with the PMI teams at five of the top ten UK brokers in the first wave. An ex-broker account manager onboards every firm in person.

Incorporate Benefits

Who. A UK employee-benefits consultancy, part of Incorporate Group.

What they bought. A £60,000 contract, signed, to build an AI-native employee-benefits policy administration system with Cluda, delivered to switchover on 27 November 2026.

Why. Their administration ran on spreadsheets and re-keying. They wanted a system that reads the policy documents and keeps the record consistent with them, built by a partner who understands broking.

Where it stands. In build, switchover 27 November 2026. It is the proof build for Cluda's system-of-record layer, which opens to brokers at £249 per user from May 2027.

Networks

Distribution is network-first rather than broker by broker. AMII is the commercial test case. The sequence from here:

  • Employee benefits in the UK first: the AMII membership and the UK's specialist EB and PMI intermediaries.
  • The global employee-benefits networks next: WBN and Brokerslink among them.
  • Then UK broker networks beyond AMII. Early-stage discussions are under way with Bravo Networks (450 broker firms) and Hedron Network for commercial lines, the first step outside employee benefits. Nothing is signed with either, and neither is counted in any figure in this data room.

How 106 member firms become paying users.

The distribution we already have, the people inside it, how each firm moves from mapped to paying, and who does the work.

As at 16 September 2026

106AMII member firms, one licence each included in year one
881People mapped by name and role across those firms
825Addressable seats at the 106 firms, against a plan of 500 users by December 2027
15Tier 1 firms holding 36% of the seats

The distribution is contracted

AMII is a one-year paid contract inside a three-year exclusive partnership: Cluda is AMII's only AI tool for policy analysis. Every member firm receives one licence in year one; additional seats are £79 per user per month, and from year two member firms buy direct. The rollout starts in November 2026, with the PMI teams at five of the top ten UK brokers in the first wave.

So the go-to-market problem is not finding buyers. It is turning a licence that every firm already has into a first real comparison, then into paid seats.

We mapped the market before the launch

Every one of the 106 firms is mapped: the employee-benefits or health team, the decision maker, and the advisers who compare policies day to day. 881 people, 398 of them daily users, 825 addressable seats. Each person carries a buying role and a LinkedIn profile, and the whole map lives in our CRM with a stage per firm.

TierFirmsPeople mappedAddressable seatsWho leadsHow
Tier 1: enterprise EB units15421295MickRelationship-led, never skips a stage, PMI team walked through in person
Tier 2: mid-size health teams17254183BelA call, a demo, the licence
Tier 3: small and specialist74206347Account managerThe AMII launch email, one call, straight to the licence
Total106881825

From mapped to paying: six stages

Every firm sits at one stage, and a firm moves only when the exit criterion is met.

StageExit criterionOwner
1. MappedDecision maker and at least one user identifiedCluda
2. ConnectingThe decision maker or a user has accepted a connection from MickMick
3. In conversationA 15-minute call held; the firm takes its licenceMick (Tier 1), Bel (Tiers 2 and 3)
4. ActivatedThe licence is issued and someone has logged inAccount manager
5. LiveThe first real comparison on a live case: the activation moment, not the loginAccount manager
6. PayingA paid seat invoicedBel; Mick for the policy administration system

A firm that goes quiet for six weeks after three touches is parked and re-enters at the next AMII event.

An ex-broker onboards every firm in person

The account manager joins in October 2026 from broking, and owns every firm from licence to live:

  • Licence day: login and a walkthrough booked on a real client case.
  • 48 hours: check-in.
  • Day 7: if there is no comparison yet, a call to find out what is in the way.
  • First comparison: ask for the second seat, ask who else in the team compares policies, capture a quote.

Activation is owned by one person, day by day, and measured weekly.

LinkedIn builds the audience before the launch

The mapped people see Cluda before the AMII launch email reaches them. This is audience-building, not outreach:

  • 15 connection requests a weekday to mapped people at the 106 firms, sent by hand, prioritised by tier. Started 14 September.
  • Three posts a week on Mick's profile, two in every three on the same three themes: the same answer every time with a page reference behind it, the Consumer Duty evidence trail, and the adviser's job once a machine does the reading.
  • Ten comments a day on posts from people at the 106 firms.
  • Every Friday the week's engagement is matched back to the map, so we know which firms are warming before we call them.

No sales messages, no automation, no paid ads, no cold email to brokers.

The forecast this feeds

The plan (section 07) counts paying users from the November rollout: 20 on policy analysis in November 2026, 40 by January 2027, then the placement and renewal workflow and the policy administration system from May 2027, reaching 500 users and £1.2M ARR by December 2027. The 106 firms alone hold 825 addressable seats, so the target does not depend on converting every firm, and the global employee-benefits networks come next.

GTM and sales is 25% of the seed (£500k): a second account manager and a sales director in the plan, travel to firms and networks, and the case-study programme.

What we will report

Weekly: firms by stage and movement, connections accepted by tier, calls held, licences issued, firms live, paid seats, and the list of firms that logged in but have not compared. Monthly to investors: firms live, active users and paid seats by rung, seats per firm, and MRR.

Ali Shahriyari is technical advisor to Cluda. Before Cluda

Before Cluda, Ali co-founded Reality Defender and served as its CTO, growing the team from himself to about forty engineers, AI researchers and data scientists, raising roughly fifty million dollars, and building the real-time deepfake detection platform that won the RSA Innovation Sandbox in 2024 and runs today at JPMorgan Chase, where its foundation model screens incoming phone calls. He holds a patent in deepfake detection.

Earlier he led product at The AI Foundation, where he helped pioneer AI digital twins and launched its first commercial applications, and held senior leadership roles at Originate, delivering large-scale systems for Fortune 500 partners.

He holds a BS and Masters in Computer Science from UCLA, went through Y Combinator in 2022, and is currently co-founder of a new company in stealth. Originally from Los Angeles, he is based in New York.

Why it matters

Reality Defender's product is trust: telling what is real from what is generated, where getting it wrong is expensive. Cluda's problem has the same shape. An insurer, a broker and a regulator all need the same answer every time, traced to the page it came from.

Aish Bhargava

AI Engineer

Insurance, automation and AI: found the problem that shaped the product, and designed the fix.

At Cluda

Aish builds the comparison pipeline behind the AMII product: document ingestion, structured extraction and the comparison engine. It runs on 70,260 product configurations and 8.27 million data points from nine insurer files, each traced to its source page.

Before joining, she reviewed Cluda's first platform. She diagnosed why the same documents could give different answers, caught leakage in how the model was prompted, and proposed moving to structured extraction at ingestion. That became the direction of the product: determinism comes from the pipeline, not the model.

Before Cluda

At Allianz Partners, part of the Allianz insurance group, Aish built automation tools and machine-learning models. At Utopia Global, a Prometheus Group company, she built a global database system supporting business operations and research.

Her published research on combining robotic process automation and AI to process financial documents accurately appeared in the International Journal of Scientific & Engineering Research. She holds a Master of Science in Information Science from the University of Pittsburgh, where she received the Anthony Debons Scholarship and the James G. Williams Award, and a BTech in Computer Science.

Why it matters

Policy wordings are financial documents at their messiest: tables, footnotes, endorsements. Aish has automated financial document processing, worked inside an insurance group, and found where Cluda's first platform broke. She built the pipeline that makes the same answer every time true.
